newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes slightly down vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes slightly down vs dollar.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed slightly weaker against the dollar on Thursday, mainly due to heavy dollar buying by two banks, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 57.08 to the dollar, near to the Central Bank's top level of 57.10, after opening at 57.05.
The Central Bank pushed down the dollar by 2.5 local cents in response to the U.S. currency's overseas easing against sterling and yen. Buying and selling prices were fixed at 55.9771 and 57.1079.
"Today was a fairly aggressive day," a Commercial Bank dealer said. "A state bank and a leading foreign bank were buying dollars, probably to cover imports."
"There was also forward demand by another foreign bank to generate money," he added.
Overnight call money opened at 26 percent, went up to about 30 percent and slumped to 14 percent at close, dealers said.
"Money rates went up when a state bank began borrowing rupees and came down when the same bank began lending," a Deutsche Bank dealer said.
